commenti.body:
> The past is both unattainable and inescapable, as are those paths not taken. In-yun, invoked semi-seriously as a pick-up line, becomes the sort of idea you convince yourself into believing, because it provides a framework to make sense of the painful gap between desire and reality. 

Such a beautiful way to put it. This movie seemed to garner a bit of criticism for being shallow or underdeveloped, but I found it to be so deep thematically, so thought-provoking. Definitely my favorite movie of last year as well.

Ive seen this movie dozens of times, the american way. Lots of hot sex, divorce, yelling, no concept of honor, or self control.

Ill skip the hollywood remake. Meryl streep comes to mind.

“ The past is both unattainable and inescapable, as are those paths not taken.”

Beautifully said. I tell myself there is only one story - there’s no such thing as what could have been. This is particularly resonant to me at this very moment - as I retrace my steps back through time, hoping to understand how I arrived at this very moment.

“They wonder, too, what they each are to one another, and whether there even is an answer to that question. But the simple fact they find themselves at this crossroads signifies that there is meaning.”

When I was a little girl, my father used to tell me that the songs I loved were written for me. I can’t escape that feeling when watching this film. So, I’ll watch it again and again. I suppose it’s personal to me, as well.

Thank you for sharing 🫶
